title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Jun 1, 2026
summary: Confirmed DRC cases reached 282 (264 Ituri, 15 Nord-Kivu, 3 Sud-Kivu) plus 9 Uganda for 291 total confirmed, with 43 confirmed deaths — a further 57 DRC cases in 48 hours as expanded mobile lab capacity continues accelerating throughput. MSF announced a major scale-up with an 80-bed ETC opening in Goma on June 1 (first patients admitted) and ETCs under construction in Ituri, Bukavu, and Lwiro, South Kivu. Four nurses were formally discharged after full Ebola recovery, bringing the total 2026 survivor count to five and providing evidence that intensive supportive care can achieve recovery without licensed BDBV therapeutics. Suspected Ebola cases in Italy (Sardinia) and Brazil (São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro) triggered international emergency protocols, though all three tested negative for Bundibugyo virus — demonstrating the global surveillance posture activated by the May 17 PHEIC declaration.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — May 31, 2026
summary: Suspected cases surpassed 1,000 by 31 May — reaching 1,077 total with 246 probable deaths — just 14 days after the WHO PHEIC declaration, a pace exceeding the 2018–2020 Kivu outbreak's early trajectory. DRC lab-confirmed cases nearly doubled from 125 (May 29) to ~225 (May 30), the fastest 48-hour confirmation rate since the outbreak began, as expanded BSL-3 mobile labs in Ituri and genuine epidemic acceleration converged. Uganda updated its confirmed count to 9. WHO Director-General Tedros visited Bunia and Kinshasa on 30 May and issued a 'maximum mobilization' emergency appeal on 31 May, calling for the $153M WHO Contingency Fund gap to be filled and an accelerated ChAdOx1 BDBV clinical trial framework finalized within 21 days. Contact tracing in DRC remains below 50% and the Mongbwalu cluster continues as a critical uncaptured transmission nucleus.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Sat May 30, 2026
summary: WHO Director-General Dr. DRC Confirmed Cases Surge to ~225 — Fastest Lab-Confirmation Rate Since Outbreak Began.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — May 29, 2026
summary: A WHO expert panel (May 28) issued a landmark ruling that Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) must not be used outside research settings for BDBV efficacy assessment, effectively halting the off-label ring vaccination campaign in Ituri and Kampala and designating ChAdOx1 BDBV (Oxford/Serum Institute) as the highest-priority vaccine candidate — Phase 1 trials possible in 2–3 months. MBP134, Maftivimab, and remdesivir were also prioritized for confirmed-case clinical trials, with obeldesivir recommended as post-exposure prophylaxis. CDC Situation Summary (May 29) confirmed 132 total lab-confirmed cases (DRC 125 + Uganda 7) after DRC MoH reconciled the suspected count to 906; confirmed deaths stand at 18. Uganda's 4-week DRC border closure entered its second day, the 25+ escaped Mongbwalu patients remain unaccounted, and contact tracing coverage in DRC remains below 45%.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — May 28, 2026
summary: The 2026 BDBV outbreak surpassed 1,205 total cases (up from 906 on May 26) as the fastest 48-hour acceleration since the PHEIC declaration recorded May 26–28; confirmed deaths rose to 18. Uganda announced a 4-week closure of all DRC border crossings on May 28 — the first such closure by any country and a direct departure from WHO IHR guidance — as 7 lab-confirmed Kampala cases drove the decision. The U.S. finalized an additional $80 million bilateral assistance package, bringing total U.S. commitment to ~$135 million. Oxford University and the Serum Institute of India confirmed their ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine could enter Phase 1 human trials within 2–3 months. DRC contact tracing coverage fell below 45% vs. the 80% containment threshold, with 25+ Mongbwalu escaped patients still unaccounted.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — May 27, 2026
summary: WHO issued a stark warning on May 27 of a 'catastrophic collision of disease and conflict' in eastern DRC, as the Bundibugyo virus outbreak outpaced response capacity. WHO Situation Report #2 (May 26) confirmed 906 suspected cases and 223 suspected deaths in DRC, with 112 lab-confirmed cases total (105 DRC + 7 Uganda — revised from preliminary 12). The Mongbwalu hospital suffered four attack waves on May 24–26, leaving 7 more suspected patients at large and forcing MSF to suspend operations there; combined with the May 23 ETU fire escapes, at least 25 suspected patients remain unaccounted. WHO warned that insecurity and mass population movements make contact tracing 'nearly impossible' across 23% of the affected zone.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Tue May 26, 2026
summary: WHO Situation Report #2: 906 Suspected Cases, 223 Deaths; Uganda Revised to 7 Lab-Confirmed. Mongbwalu Hospital Hit by Four Attack Waves — 7 More BDBV Patients Escape; MSF Suspends Operations.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — May 25, 2026
summary: Uganda's Bundibugyo virus case count jumped from 5 to 12 confirmed cases within 48 hours, with 147 contacts now under monitoring. DRC has 900+ suspected cases across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, and Sud-Kivu provinces. All 18 suspected Ebola patients who fled the Mongbwalu ETU fire (May 23) remain unaccounted, complicating contact tracing. Oxford University confirmed its ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine is 6–9 months from human trials — no licensed Bundibugyo vaccine exists. The US pledged to fund up to 50 Ebola response clinics in DRC and a total of ~$55M in bilateral aid; the EU has committed €15M.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — May 24, 2026
summary: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak has escalated to PHEIC status, with WHO making an unprecedented declaration on May 17 without prior Emergency Committee consultation. Suspected cases have surged to ~750 across three DRC provinces (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu) with 177 suspected deaths, while Uganda confirmed 5 imported cases in Kampala. Attacks on Ebola treatment centers in Rwampara (May 21) and Mongbwalu (May 22) — the latter causing 18 suspected patients to flee into the community — represent critical setbacks to containment. No licensed Bundibugyo-specific vaccine exists, and WHO has raised DRC's risk level to 'Very High.'

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Sat May 23, 2026
summary: Uganda confirmed three additional cases of Bundibugyo virus disease, bringing the country's total to five. US Reroutes Passengers from DRC, Uganda, South Sudan to 3 Airports for Ebola Screening.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Fri May 22, 2026
summary: The WHO IHR Emergency Committee issued formal temporary recommendations following its first meeting, advising affected countries and all states parties on the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) epidemic. Angry residents arrived at the MSF-operated Ebola Treatment Unit in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, on the night of 22 May and set fire to a tent housing suspected and confirmed Ebola cases. US Embassy Kampala Issues Health Alert as WHO Raises DRC Risk to Very High.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Thu May 21, 2026
summary: Protesters Set Rwampara Ebola Treatment Unit on Fire in Ituri Province. First South Kivu Case Confirmed — Outbreak Spreads to Third DRC Province.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Wed May 20, 2026

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Tue May 19, 2026
summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus convened the first meeting of the IHR Emergency Committee regarding the Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic in DRC and Uganda.

title: Ebola Outbreak Tracker Update — Mon May 18, 2026
